Write node:test behaviour tests for the browser script of a meeting-room booking app in /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc, using the existing fake-DOM harness. Load the Skill `tdd-workflow` if available (else skip). Node 22 built-ins only. READ FIRST: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/spec.md section "Page" (the authority), /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/frontend-page.md, the script /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/public/app.js, and the harness /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs: `loadPage({fetchImpl?})` → {document, el(id), calls, flush}; each calls[i] has url, options, jsonCalls, resolve(status, body), resolveBadJson(status), reject(), resolveWith(responseObject); `el(id).dispatch(type)` returns the event (defaultPrevented); `listTexts(ul)` → per li {text, button:{type,text,disabled}, childCount, nodes}. Gotcha: objects made inside the vm have another Object.prototype — compare options.headers / parsed bodies via JSON round trip (JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))) before deepEqual. Do NOT edit public/* or the harness; small local helpers in the test files are fine (e.g. to find the Cancel button node: el('booking-list').childNodes[i].childNodes[1]). Create: 1. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/page-load-list.test.mjs — rooms, list rendering, overlapping fetches, filter, show-all. 2. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/page-actions.test.mjs — submit and cancel flows. Rules: `import { test, describe } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`. Exact equality for every text the spec names ('Could not reach the server.', 'Request failed.', 'No bookings.', 'Cancel', etc.). Each test loads its own page. Files under 400 lines, functions under 50 lines; table-driven where it fits. No console.log. After resolving a call, `await flush()`. Run with `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc && node --test test/` until green. If a test fails because the SCRIPT violates the spec, keep the test and report it. A request's method: accept options === undefined or options.method === 'GET' for GETs (helper `methodOf(call) = call.options?.method ?? 'GET'`). page-load-list.test.mjs: - At load, synchronously after loadPage: calls.length === 2; calls[0].url === '/api/rooms' GET; calls[1].url === '/api/bookings' GET (list fetch starts without waiting for rooms). - Rooms 200 {rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']} → #room has exactly 3 child nodes, each tagName 'OPTION' with value and textContent equal to the room, in order; #error stays ''. - Rooms error status: 500 {error:'boom'} → #error 'boom', #room has 0 children. 404 {error: 5} → 'Request failed.'; 500 [] → 'Request failed.'; 500 'text' → 'Request failed.'; 500 null → 'Request failed.'; 201 {rooms:[...]} (wrong success status for GET) → #error shows 'Request failed.' and #room empty. No reply: reject() → 'Could not reach the server.', #room empty; resolveBadJson(200) → 'Could not reach the server.'; resolveBadJson(500) → 'Could not reach the server.'. - List render: reply 200 {bookings:[{id:2,room:'Cosmos',title:'Standup',date:'2026-11-04',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'},{id:1,room:'Aurora',title:'x',date:'2026-11-03',start:'13:00',end:'14:30'}]} → exactly 2
  • (tagName 'LI'), in REPLY order; each li has exactly 2 child nodes: node 0 is a text node (nodeType 3) with data exactly '2026-11-04 09:00-10:00 Cosmos: Standup' / '2026-11-03 13:00-14:30 Aurora: x' (no trailing space), node 1 a BUTTON with type 'button', text 'Cancel', not disabled. - Title with surrounding spaces in the reply is shown unchanged (' x ' → '... Aurora: x '). - Empty → exactly one li with exactly one child: text node 'No bookings.'. - List error status leaves the list: first render one booking, then trigger another fetch (filter change) and reply 500 {error:'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'} → #error exactly that and the list unchanged (same li text). Reply 404 {} → 'Request failed.'. No reply (reject) → 'Could not reach the server.', list unchanged. resolveBadJson(200) → 'Could not reach the server.'. - Successful list fetch leaves #error alone: make rooms fail with 500 {error:'boom'} first, then list 200 → #error still 'boom'. - Overlapping list fetches (only the last started counts): (a) initial list call A pending; change filter → call B; resolve B 200 [X] → list X; then resolve A 200 [Y] → list still X. (b) resolve A first with [Y] while B pending → list not changed to Y (still initial empty: childNodes length 0), then B [X] → X. (c) earlier fetch error status after later success → #error unchanged ''. (d) earlier fetch reject → #error unchanged. (e) earlier fetch error while later still pending → #error unchanged and list unchanged; then later succeeds → rendered. (f) three overlapping: only the third's outcome used. - Filter: set el('filter-date').value = '2026-11-03', dispatch('change') → exactly one new call, url exactly '/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03', GET. Value passed unchanged: value 'a b&c' → url '/api/bookings?date=a b&c'. dispatch('input') → no new call. Value '' then change → url '/api/bookings'. - Show all: filter value '2026-11-03', show-all dispatch('click') → filter value exactly '' and exactly one new call with url '/api/bookings'. page-actions.test.mjs (first resolve rooms 200 and the initial list 200 {bookings:[]} unless the test needs otherwise): - Submit: set #room value 'Cosmos', #title ' Team sync ', #date '2026-11-03', #start '09:00', #end '10:00'; ev = el('booking-form').dispatch('submit') → ev.defaultPrevented true; el('book').disabled true synchronously; exactly one new call: url '/api/bookings', options.method 'POST', JSON-roundtripped options.headers deepEqual exactly {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, JSON.parse(options.body) deepEqual exactly {room:'Cosmos',title:' Team sync ',date:'2026-11-03',start:'09:00',end:'10:00'} (title NOT trimmed; exactly 5 keys). - No client-side checks: all fields empty (room select with no options → '') still sends POST with all values ''. - Submit while Book disabled: second dispatch('submit') while the first is pending → defaultPrevented true and no new call. Also if el('book').disabled = true set by the test, submit sends nothing. - 201: resolve(201, {...booking}) → book enabled; #title value ''; #room/#date/#start/#end keep values; #error '' (preset #error.textContent = 'old' before); exactly one new list call '/api/bookings' (or with ?date= when filter set — test with filter '2026-11-03' too → url '/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'). - Error status: 409 {error:'room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00'} → #error exactly that; title kept; no new call; book enabled. 400 {} → 'Request failed.'. 500 {error:['x']} → 'Request failed.'. 200 {} for POST (not 201) → error status → 'Request failed.'. - No reply: reject → 'Could not reach the server.', title kept, no list call, book enabled. resolveBadJson(201) → 'Could not reach the server.' and no list call. - Re-enable as soon as request settles, before anything else: (1) resolveWith({status:201, json: () => p}) where p is a promise you control → after flush book still disabled (body not arrived); resolve p → enabled. (2) Use a custom fetchImpl (loadPage({fetchImpl})) that records el('book').disabled at the moment a list fetch starts after a 201 → recorded false. (3) For an error status, before resolving redefine #error's textContent setter on that element instance (Object.defineProperty(errorEl,'textContent',{set(v){record(book.disabled); ...store}, get(){...}})) and assert book was already enabled when #error was set. - Cancel: list rendered with booking id 7 (and another id 8); click the first li's Cancel button (node.dispatch('click')) → that button disabled true; new call url exactly '/api/bookings/7', options.method 'DELETE'. resolve(204) → button enabled, #error '' (preset 'old'), exactly one new list call; jsonCalls on the DELETE call is 0. 404 {error:'booking not found'} → #error 'booking not found', button enabled, one new list call. 500 'x' → 'Request failed.' and list fetched again. reject → 'Could not reach the server.', button enabled, NO new list call. Button re-enabled before the list refetch starts (record via custom fetchImpl) and before #error is set. - Cancel then list refetch honours the filter value (filter '2026-11-04' → '/api/bookings?date=2026-11-04'). Final message: files, number of tests, pass/fail, any spec violation. Keep it short.

content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2.
